content: Capillary refill refers to the rate at which blood returns to empty capillaries. Capillary refill time (CRT) is specifically defined as the duration it takes for color to return to an external capillary bed after pressure has been applied to cause blanching. To measure CRT, one can elevate the hand above heart level, press on the soft pad of a finger until it turns white, and then release the pressure while noting the time it takes for the color to return. Under normal conditions, capillary refill time is typically less than 2 seconds. In newborn infants, CRT can be assessed by pressing on the sternum with a finger or thumb for five seconds and observing the time required for the color to return after releasing the pressure. The upper normal limit for capillary refill time in neonates is also 2 seconds. In animals, CRT can be evaluated by pressing on their gums, as the sternum is often covered with fur or otherwise inaccessible. A prolonged capillary refill time may indicate shock, dehydration, or reduced peripheral perfusion. However, it is widely recognized that this test is influenced by numerous external factors and, as such, should not be solely relied upon as a definitive diagnostic tool.
